# Celeris Cookbook

> Runnable examples and guides for the Celeris API. celeris-1 is a diffusion
> model served through an OpenAI-compatible API: replies arrive as one burst,
> typically in 250 to 300 ms for short outputs, inside a 4096-token window
> with max_tokens as a multiple of 256 between 256 and 1024.

The published site is at https://docs.celeris.ai/cookbook/. Every example is
a standalone directory that runs with CELERIS_BASE_URL and CELERIS_API_KEY
set. The index of examples is registry.yaml.

## Guides

- [Understanding latency](guides/latency.md): metrics, the one-burst
  delivery model, token-window budgeting, what becomes possible at 300 ms.
- [The cascade](guides/cascade.md): fast model in the hot path, larger model
  refining or escalating asynchronously.
- [Shell tasks with the CLI](guides/cli-shell-tasks.md): semantic operations
  in shell pipes with the official CLI.

## Examples

- [Getting started](examples/getting-started/getting-started.ipynb): first
  request with the OpenAI SDK, budgeting helpers, burst timing.
- [Streaming chatbot](examples/chatbot/README.md): web chat measuring
  time-to-first-token in the browser.
- [Instant regex](examples/instant-suggest/README.md): artifact synthesized
  on every typing pause with in-browser validation.
- [Real-time ticket routing](examples/realtime-classification/README.md):
  classification in the request path at about 260 ms median.
- [Guardrails](examples/guardrails/README.md): an allow/block/flag gate fast
  enough for every request.
- [Agent latency](examples/agent-latency/README.md): how per-step latency
  compounds over agent steps, measured.
- [Alert triage agent](examples/alert-triage-agent/README.md): multi-step
  tool loop with a structured verdict.
- [Benchmark harness](examples/benchmark/README.md): latency percentiles,
  reliability counters, correctness scoring against your own workspace.
- [Next.js on Vercel](examples/nextjs-vercel/README.md): managed-secret
  deployment pattern for TypeScript.
- [FastAPI on Fly.io](examples/fastapi-fly/README.md): managed-secret
  deployment pattern for Python.
